4. Workmanship and Finish 

4.1 The trocar shanl^ shall be central and its point shall lie on the axis. 

4.2 The trocar edges sh$l be well-cut, clean, sharp and free from nicks, feathers and pits.

4.J Handle shall be hollow ind shall bo fitted to the trocar shank by silver soldering. The silver solder- 
ing shall be sound and neat* 

4.4 The cannula shall smoothly fit the trocar. The edge of the tip of the cannula shall be sharp and the 
tip shall be silt and sprung In to snap on the neck of the trocar. When the cannula is snapped on to the 
trocar neck the cannula tip shall fit snugly to facilitate smooth entry of the trocar-cahnula assembly. 

4.5 The Instrument shall be balanced and shall have a good feel. 

4.6 All edges except the trocar point and cannula tip shall be even, rounded and nowhere sharp. All 
surfaces shall be smooth and free from burrs, pits, cracks and other surface flaws. 

4.7 The trocar shank, cannula and the handle when made of stainless steel shall be passivated and polished 
bright. The adapter and the handle when made of brass shall be placed chromium over nickel and the 
placing shall conform to Service Grade No. 2 of IS: 4827- 1968 'Specification for electroplated coatings of 
nickel and chromium on copper and copper alloys'. 

5. Heat Treatment— The trocar porcion shall be hardened and tempered to a hardness of 400 
to 500 HV. 

6. Teats 

6.1 Performance Test — Take a piece of cardboard IS mm chick. Hold the cardboard piece in such a way 
that ic is supported by chumb and firsc two fingers. The fingers shall support the cardboard piece to enable 
the crocar co punch through the cardboard. Keeping che trocar pome againsc che cardboard, push the- tro- 
car by hand) to make a hole in che cardboard. The hole shall be cleanly made wich a moderate push 
of the hand. The trocar tip and edges shall noc get damaged during che tesc. 

6.2 Flexibility Test — Hold che crocar, wichouc che cannula, from che handle in a vice in such a way chat 
the encire lengch of che crocar shank lies oucside che vice. Apply a force ac che cip of che crocar co deflect 
ft chrough 25 mm from ics original posicion. Release che force. The tip shall return co its original 
posicion and shall noc have acquired a new sec. 

6.3 Corrosion Resistance Test for Stainless Steel Components — Scrub che sample wich soap and warm water, 
rinse in hoc wacer and chen dip In 95 percenc echyl alcohol. Dry che sample. Immerse In copper sulphace 
solution ac room temperature for 6 minutes and wash off wich fresh water or wee cotton wool. 

Prepare the solution as follows: 

Copper sulphace (CuS04.5HjtO) 4*0 g 

Sulphuric acid (H 2 SO«) (spgr 1-84) 100 g 

Distilled water [see IS : 1070-1960 Specification 90*0 ml 

for wacer, distilled quality ( reWsed) ] 

No red stains or spocs on the sample shall be allowed, but dulling of che polished surface may be 
permicced. 

7. Marking — Mark with the following: 

a) Manufacturer's name, initials or recognized trade-mark; and 

b) Words 'Stainless Steel ' on the trocar shank and cannula. 

7.1 ISI Certification Marking— Details available from the Indian Scandards Inscicution, New Delhi I. > 

8. Packing — As agreed to between the purchaser and the supplier ensuring that che trocar and cannula 
tips are suitably protected.
